Designing a superconducting qubit to realize specific Hamiltonian parameters typically requires iterating through a time and compute-intensive forward loop in which the designer chooses a layout geometry, simulates it, extracts circuit parameters such as capacitances, and refines the geometry. We study the inverse version of this task using a neural-network workflow that maps target Hamiltonian parameters directly to component-level layout parameters, which we subsequently demonstrate on a planar transmon layout. During training, we pair the inverse model with a frozen forward surrogate model and evaluate the loss in Hamiltonian space rather than in layout-parameter space. item.title: Prediction of solvent aggregation in CO 2 -loaded aqueous amines using machine learning molecular dynamics simulations
item.description:
📚 The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue
Aggregation of ion pairs formed during CO 2 capture may govern absorption thermodynamics and kinetics, but it is often overestimated by fixed-charge classical force fields. Here, we demonstrate the promise of graph neural network interatomic potentials, which offer quantum-level accuracy, for directly evaluating the aggregation tendencies of ionic products in CO 2 -loaded aqueous amine solutions.

item.description:

Accurately predicting the energy and relevant properties of molecules and complex crystalline systems remains a cornerstone of computational materials science. While density functional theory (DFT) offers high accuracy, its computational cost scales prohibitively for large-scale materials. In this work, we present a comprehensive, first-principles-derived database of two-atom interaction potentials and interatomic forces to accelerate the property prediction via physics-informed machine learning. Computed using spin-polarized DFT via the GPAW package, the database encompasses all 2346 possible atomic pairs generated from 68 unique elements as a function of interatomic distance. item.title: PolyFKAN: Integrating Fourier-KAN layers into graph neural networks for polymer property prediction
item.description:
📚 The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue
Graph neural networks have become a central tool for polymer property prediction, but their fixed activation functions can impose a low-pass spectral bias that smooths over the sharp, multi-scale structure–property variations that distinguish chemically similar polymers. We address this limitation with PolyFKAN, a multitask graph-learning architecture that augments the prediction head of a polyGNN backbone with Fourier Kolmogorov–Arnold network layers. PolyFKAN represents edge-wise activations as truncated Fourier series and couples the resulting spectral branch to the standard multilayer perceptron (MLP) pathway through a bounded residual gate, thereby increasing functional expressivity without disrupting the learned graph embeddings. We introduce Platonic Projection Structures (PPS), an operator-theoretic framework for analyzing observability in representation learning systems. Rather than treating observable outputs as direct reflections of latent representations, PPS models observation as a geometry induced by a self-adjoint positive semidefinite operator acting on a latent Hilbert space. Within PPS, a system is represented as a triple (H, Π, O), where Hdenotes a latent representation space, Π ⪰0 is an observation operator, and O(v) = ⟨v, Πv⟩defines an induced observable quantity. item.description:
📚 The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue
We study the structural, thermophysical, and dynamical properties of molten MgCl 2 over a wide temperature range using Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics (AIMD) and molecular dynamics simulations based on machine-learning interaction potentials (MLIPs). MLIPs can achieve near-AIMD accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost, enabling simulations of larger systems and longer timescales. This opens up the possibility of studying the system under out-of-equilibrium conditions, which in turn allows for the calculation of physical properties, such as the thermal conductivity or viscosity, that cannot be obtained reliably for the typical time and length scales accessible to AIMD. item.title: Can Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials Capture Small Polarons? A Geometry-Based Benchmark in Transition-Metal Oxides
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Vladislav Korostelev, Pjotrs Žguns, Konstantin Klyukin
arXiv:2610.17352v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Small polarons, formed when excess electrons become localized through lattice distortions, play a critical role in charge transport, catalysis, and degradation processes in transition-metal (TM) oxides. Whether universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs), which lack explicit electronic degrees of freedom, can describe them remains unclear. item.description:

👤 Anton Z. Ni, Joonho Lee
arXiv:2610.17226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are trained on gas-phase data, which limits their use for chemistry in solution. Here, we introduce AnySolv, a transferable implicit solvation potential that provides solvent-dependent energy and force corrections to existing gas-phase potentials without retraining them. It is trained on 1.4 million solvation energies and forces computed with density functional theory (DFT) and SMD in 36 solvents, spanning charged, open-shell, and transition-state structures. Because solvents are represented by continuous physical descriptors, AnySolv supports 179 solvents, including those absent from training. arXiv:2610.14774v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly expected to orchestrate diverse tools over long-horizon tasks. Existing agents typically use Direct Tool Calling (DTC), where the model invokes tools sequentially, and tool responses accumulate in the model context, which can lead to context rot and orchestration breakdown. arXiv:2610.17366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: General-purpose molecular dynamics software supports diverse interatomic potentials and simulation requirements.
